precepts.text: And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them.
precepts.point: For there are set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David. Pray for the peace of Jerusalem: they shall prosper that love thee. Some of y'all busy praying for Haiti, praying for Puerto Rico, praying for Mexico, praying for America. But the Bible said pray for Jerusalem. Remember, Jerusalem's a people before it's a place. We are Jerusalem. Pray for us. We're not supposed to be praying, stop the war over there; no, we got to move them out of our land so that we can go back home.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
David says of Jerusalem, “For there are set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David.” John saw those thrones: “And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them.”

Thrones set, people sitting on them, and judgment given to them. And who are they? The souls “beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God, and which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands; and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.”

The thrones of judgment in the psalm are real thrones in the kingdom, where the faithful reign with Christ. That is the Jerusalem the tribes go up to, and that is why we pray for its peace: it is a people before it is a place, and those thrones belong to us.

precepts.text: And they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years. The seventh day Sabbath represents us resting and reigning with Christ; that is what every seventh day is rehearsing.
precepts.point: Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief. Rest is entered by labour; that is the paradox the wilderness generation never accepted.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
If one day with the Lord is a thousand years, what is the seventh day rest? Revelation shows it: “And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them: and I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God, and which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands; and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.”

They lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years. That is going into the rest. The seventh day Sabbath represents us resting with Christ, and every seventh day is rehearsing it.

The rest promised in Hebrews is not the land Joshua brought us into, and not only the one day a week before going back to labour in Esau’s system. It is the eternal reign with Christ when he comes back, sitting on thrones with judgment given to us, rulership over our enemies. “There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.” Seven represents completion, and the seventh day points to that completion: the kingdom and the thousand years with Christ.

precepts.text: Thrones, and judgment given unto them, the souls beheaded for the witness of Jesus who had not worshipped the beast nor received his mark, and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years. That is the third temple set up.
precepts.point: The glory of Lebanon, the fir, pine, and box, shall beautify the place of my sanctuary; Lebanon and its famous trees belong to the Israelites. The sons of them that afflicted thee shall come bending, and all that despised thee shall bow at the soles of thy feet and call thee the city of the Lord, the Zion of the Holy One of Israel. That is what Revelation 3:9 said. The third temple is under Christ, not under Edom.
precepts.why:
Still on the third temple: “And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them”. Power was given unto them.

Then: “and I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God”: the martyred. Then: “and which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands”: the mark of sin, that lets you know it is somebody in these last days, who would not support the beast.

Then: “and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years”. Notice the top of it: thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them. This is the third temple being built up. We are going to reign with Christ for a thousand years.

That is why Isaiah 60 ends with the ones who afflicted us bowing: “all they that despised thee shall bow themselves down at the soles of thy feet; and they shall call thee, The city of the Lord, The Zion of the Holy One of Israel.” It is the same thing Revelation 3:9 said. The third temple is under Christ, not what the Christians make of Daniel 9.

precepts.text: I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them, the souls beheaded for the witness of Jesus who had not worshipped the beast nor his image nor received his mark, and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.
precepts.point: Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities; thine eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, at rest, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down, not one stake removed nor any cord broken. You will never take down Jerusalem again. Psalms 46:4-7, God is in the midst of her, she shall not be moved; the heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved, he uttered his voice, the earth melted; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Psalms 48:1-2, beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, the city of the great King.
precepts.why:
“And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them”: the thrones of judgment of Psalms 122.

Then “I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God”: that is great tribulation. They are the ones “which had not worshipped the beast”: which had not worshipped this white man, this kingdom. Nor “his image”: his religion, his politics. And they had not “received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands”: they did not receive his lies in their foreheads, in their minds.

And so “they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.” Those who come through great tribulation without bowing to the beast are the ones who sit on the thrones in the Jerusalem Isaiah 33:20 describes, the tabernacle that shall not be taken down.

precepts.text: A great white throne, and him that sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away; nobody opens their mouth against Christ. 2 Corinthians 5:10, we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; John 5:22, the Father judgeth no man but hath committed all judgment unto the Son. The dead, small and great, were judged out of the books according to their works, whether in God's laws or against them, Ecclesiastes 12:14, every secret thing, whether good or evil. The sea, death, and hell gave up their dead; death and hell were cast into the lake of fire, the second death, and whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast in, the nations with them.
precepts.point: For, behold, the Lord cometh out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity; the earth also shall disclose her blood, and shall no more cover her slain. Jeremiah 51:49: as Babylon hath caused the slain of Israel to fall, so at Babylon shall fall the slain of all the earth. Revelation 18:24: in her was found the blood of prophets, and of saints, and of all that were slain upon the earth. The judgment on this kingdom will be the worst of all.
precepts.why:
“For, behold, the Lord cometh out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity: the earth also shall disclose her blood, and shall no more cover her slain.” Revelation 20 shows that day of judgment.

“And I saw a great white throne, and him that sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away; and there was found no place for them.” That is Christ, in full power, and nobody opens their damn mouth against him. We thought it was the Father judging us, but it is Christ: “we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad.” And “the Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son.”

“And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God; and the books were opened”: this is everybody, and the books are the Bible. “And another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.” As Ecclesiastes says, “God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.” We are judged according to our works, whether we were in God's laws or against God's laws.

“And the sea gave up the dead which were in it; and death and hell delivered up the dead which were in them.” That is what Isaiah 26 said: the earth shall no more cover her slain. Hell is the grave; those that died in the graves were given up, “and they were judged every man according to their works.”

“And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death.” Death is finished at that point. And what goes with death and hell? The nations: “whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.” That includes all the nations. The Lord comes out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth, and this is where that punishment ends.

precepts.text: The dead are judged out of the books according to their works, set beside the book of life.
precepts.point: The righteous are saved by being judged out of the book of life alongside the record of their works. Christianity is worse than crack cocaine because it tells our people to believe on Christ while keeping no commandments, setting them on the path to destruction.

note.label: Psalm 7: David's Prayer for Deliverance in the Last Days

precepts.why:
“My defence is of God, which saveth the upright in heart.” To be upright in heart is to be righteous, and John shows how the righteous are saved: “And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God; and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.”

The dead are judged out of the books according to their works, set beside the book of life. Salvation is not by belief alone; the record of your works stands next to the book of life.

That is why Christianity is worse than crack cocaine. It tells our people to believe on Christ while keeping no commandments, setting them on the path to destruction, when the judgment is according to works. God saves the upright in heart, those whose works show it.

precepts.text: A great white throne, and from the face of him that sat on it the earth and heaven fled away.
precepts.point: Everyone will flee at the presence of Jesus Christ. Even the Romans who pierced him will be back on the scene and will wail because of him.

note.label: Psalm 9: I Will Praise the Lord With My Whole Heart

precepts.why:
David says, “When mine enemies are turned back, they shall fall and perish at thy presence. For thou hast maintained my right and my cause; thou satest in the throne judging right.” John saw that throne: “And I saw a great white throne, and him that sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away; and there was found no place for them.”

A great white throne, and from the face of him that sat on it the earth and heaven fled away. Everyone will flee at the presence of Jesus Christ. That is the enemies falling and perishing at his presence while he sits in the throne judging right, and it is why David praises the Lord with his whole heart.

precepts.text: The dead were judged out of the books according to their works, and whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.
precepts.point: Add iniquity unto their iniquity, and let them not come into Thy righteousness; let them be blotted out of the book of the living and not be written with the righteous. That is a heavy statement.
precepts.why:
“Let them be blotted out of the book of the living, and not be written with the righteous.” That is a heavy statement. John sees what it means: “I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God; and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.” Then: “whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.”

David asks that the Most High pour out his indignation on them that persecute him whom he has smitten, add iniquity unto their iniquity and let them not come into his righteousness. This is why blindness happened to the southern Kingdom leadership that forsook Christ; their eyes were darkened and their table became a snare, as you read in Romans 11. To be blotted out of the book of the living is to not be found written in the book of life, and that is the lake of fire.

precepts.text: Satan being loosed at the end of the thousand years is the same moment this prophecy against Gog describes.
precepts.point: This is the same setting as Revelation 20, when Satan is loosed in both the spiritual and the physical form: the spiritual demon Satan and the physical Esau. The Most High smites the bow out of Gog's left hand and causes his arrows to fall out of his right hand, so no weapon formed against Israel will prosper. He smacks their weapons out of their hand and their weapon is for naught.

note.label: Ezekiel 39: The Fall of Gog and the Gathering of Israel

precepts.why:
“And when the thousand years are expired, Satan shall be loosed out of his prison”. That is the same moment this prophecy against Gog describes: after Christ has taken down the other nations and Israel is in their land.

Satan is loosed in both the spiritual and the physical form: the spiritual demon Satan, and the physical Esau, Gog the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, coming up from the north parts upon the mountains of Israel.

And the Most High is against him. He smites the bow out of Gog's left hand and causes his arrows to fall out of his right hand. He smacks their weapons out of their hand and their weapon is for naught; no weapon formed against Israel will prosper.

“But the rest of the dead lived not again until the thousand years were finished.” You know who that rest of the dead is: your mothers and fathers, sisters and brothers, friends, uncles and aunts that have rejected this truth, these words of these scriptures. They died in sin. Some of the women say, but my mama read the Bible all her life. Yeah, with that white image of the beast on the wall back there. You ain't fooling nobody, sister: your mama was the devil.

Having rejected the truth. That is not talking about during the time of Marcus Garvey, or even MLK; the truth wasn't out like it is now. But now, with all these men and women, the truth is out, so now we can clearly say you heard the truth and you died in your sins. “This is the first resurrection.”

points: So if you haven't read, this is judgment day. This is the day that you stand before the Most High. It says, and the books were opened.
And another book was opened, which is the book of life. So we understand the book of life is the Bible.

According to their works. Notice it says it's according to your works, not according to your feelings, not according to your beliefs, not according to your opinions. According to the works. What works have you done in the short time that you have?

The works are going into righteous works: keeping God's laws, honouring him on his high holy days, honouring the Sabbath days, eating clean foods, staying away from unclean foods, putting on your fringes, being a representative, teaching your people. Have you done these works? Or are you secure and safe in the lies that are being told?
So the time that you've been given, the short time that we've been given, is for you to put in works: works of righteousness, works of keeping God's laws, in order to get the kingdom.
